paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Elijah asks, "How long will you waver between two opinions?" (1 Kings 18:21), and the people don't answer a word. Standing in the middle feels safe, but it's just a slow way of not deciding. The passage says the LORD isn't a backup you keep next to the other options, and that's a question for every baker today, too.

Now look at the two altars. Baal's prophets shout, leap and cut themselves, and "there was no response; no one answered, no one paid attention" (1 Kings 18:29). Then Elijah prays one simple prayer, and "the fire of the LORD fell" (1 Kings 18:38). Friend, that's the difference between a god somebody makes up and the LORD who answers, and it's why all the people say, "The LORD, He is God!" (1 Kings 18:39).

And don't miss the rain at the end. Elijah says there is the sound of a heavy rain (1 Kings 18:41), and then he keeps sending his servant back to look until a cloud as small as a man's hand shows up (1 Kings 18:43-44). I think that's an invitation to keep trusting when the sky still looks empty. The LORD is God, so follow Him with your whole heart, and keep watching for what He's bringing, friend.
